title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system for customizing investment type based on the potential investors' demographics and feedback
authors: Asemi, A.; Asemi, A.; Ko, A.
tldr: An ANFIS-based recommender system uses investor demographic data and feedback to suggest investment types via K-Means clustering and fuzzy inference with 1296 generated rules.
problem_and_motivation: Existing investment recommender systems focus on stock portfolios, hedge funds, or resource allocation but lack models that recommend investment types based on potential investors' demographics using ANFIS. No prior study has developed a demographic-driven ANFIS investment recommender system that combines expert knowledge with investor feedback.
approach: Collected 1542 responses from a Hungarian online investment questionnaire capturing six demographic variables and investment type preferences.
Applied K-Means clustering in JMP to group investment types into three clusters based on stock, pension, bond, and other product preferences.
Implemented a Sugeno-type ANFIS model in MATLAB R2022b using six demographic inputs and three investment type clusters as output.
Trained the ANFIS network with a hybrid optimization method over 3 epochs using 1542 training data pairs.
Supplemented system-generated fuzzy rules with expert knowledge rules and investor feedback for iterative improvement.
findings: num: Three investment clusters identified: 592, 406, and 340 respondents respectively.
num: DemographicANFIS network comprises 2647 nodes and 1365 parameters (1296 linear, 69 nonlinear).
num: System generated 1296 fuzzy IF-THEN rules for investment recommendations.
num: Average testing error of 0.86683 after training convergence at epoch 3.
num: 1542 training data pairs used with Gaussian membership functions across 6 demographic inputs.
Cluster 1 (592 respondents) favors government securities and mutual funds with no recent stock market activity.
Cluster 2 (406 respondents) includes active stock investors who regularly monitor performance and hold government bonds.
Cluster 3 (340 respondents) comprises active stock investors without government bond holdings.

definitions.definition: Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System, a hybrid model combining neural networks with fuzzy logic for inference.
Fuzzy Inference System, a framework using fuzzy rules, membership functions, and reasoning to produce outputs.
Membership Function, defines the degree to which an input belongs to a fuzzy set.
A type of fuzzy inference system using polynomial consequents in IF-THEN rules.
An unsupervised clustering algorithm that partitions data into k groups based on distance to centroids.
Sum of Squared Errors, a metric used to evaluate cluster quality in K-Means.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces a novel ANFIS-based investment recommender system that combines K-Means clustering with fuzzy inference to classify investors into behavioral profiles based on six demographic variables.
directly_justifies: None of these studies have specifically focused on developing a recommender system for the type or product of investment based on demographics using ANFIS.
The proposed system categorizes customers based on six demographic traits using six input factors with three investment type clusters as output.
1542 training data pairs were used to train the ANFIS system with a hybrid optimization method over 3 epochs.
The system generated 1296 fuzzy IF-THEN rules supplemented by expert knowledge rules.
The ANFIS system categorizes investors into three clusters with 592, 406, and 340 respondents respectively.
limits: Paper focuses on investment type recommendation, not personal budgeting, expense categorization, or savings management.
Demographic data limited to Hungarian respondents, restricting direct relevance to Filipino financial demographics.
No discussion of mobile-first design, offline-first architecture, or on-device inference.
No evaluation of user trust, consent management, or data portability beyond basic data collection.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 5 was flagged as high relevance since the paper profiles investors into clusters using ANFIS and K-Means. Domain 4 received medium relevance for literature review. Domain 12 received medium relevance for system evaluation.

limitations: Limited to six demographic variables as system inputs, excluding personality traits and financial attitudes.
Only three investment type clusters used as output, restricting recommendation granularity.
No comparative evaluation against alternative algorithms.
Dataset from a single Hungarian survey may limit generalizability.
Training error of 0.8668 is reported without baseline comparisons.
